# bd-apvhh — how many findings each inventory rule OWNS.
#
# `classify_finding` takes the FIRST rule whose fragment appears in a finding's
# +/-4 context window, so a rule's blast radius is not visible from its text. A
# fragment that owns 3 sites today and 30 next month has silently become a
# different rule, and nothing said so.
#
# This ledger makes that visible. The gate fails in BOTH directions:
#   - a rule owning MORE than its declared count absorbed sites nobody reviewed;
#   - a rule owning FEWER is stale and the number must come down.
# One arm without the other is how a ledger decays into decoration.
#
# A count of 0 is a rule that classifies NOTHING. Those are dead weight, not
# coverage -- but "owns zero" is TWO defects and this line originally named only
# the first (bd-epvc1, measured 2026-09-17: 33 of 331 rules own zero):
#   - SHADOWED (6): the fragment really does match findings and an EARLIER rule
#     wins them. Check whether the absorber's reason covers what it absorbed.
#   - DEAD FRAGMENT (27): the fragment matches no finding at all, shadowed or
#     not. Eight of those are must_fix rules, each naming a follow-up bead while
#     watching nothing, which is the actionable half.
#
# WHAT A GREEN HERE DOES NOT MEAN. Both arms fire when a count MOVES. Neither
# can fire on shadowing that ALREADY EXISTED when these numbers were recorded,
# because they were recorded from current behaviour -- an absorbing rule's count
# was written down with the absorption already inside it. So this ledger
# certifies today's shadowing as correct and guards only tomorrow's. It is a
# ratchet pinned to the day it was taken. That is a bound on the green, not a
# reason to distrust the arms; the pre-existing shadowing is bd-epvc1's job.
#
# Recorded 2026-09-17 against the detector at that commit. Regenerate by
# reading the gate, never by hand-adjusting a number to make it pass.
#
# Format: <count>\t<rule id>

# RETIRED (bd-epvc1), each owned 0 while naming a CLOSED follow-up bead:
#   NSF-CASS-PIPE-READ         bd-sos5.2   closed
#   NSF-HOOK-INSTALLER-JSON    bd-sos5.3   closed
#   NSF-CLI-CERTIFICATE-JSON   bd-sos5.3   closed
#   NSF-CLI-DEMO-AUDIT         bd-sos5.4   closed

# bd-apvhh 2026-09-17: the first FUNCTION-SCOPED group rules. The count is

# optional projection fields in from_ledger(), two of which are the identical

# two-directional.

# bd-apvhh burn-down tranche 3: src/mesh/team.rs and src/core/resume.rs, taken
# because they are where the answer could come back NOT allowed. It did once,
# and NSF-MESH-TEAM-JOIN-SYNC-OWN-ORIGIN-SWALLOWED is this burn-down's first
# must_fix (bd-1jpg7, a fail-open on the no-echo ingest guard).
#
# THREE OF THESE SEVEN WERE WRONG ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT and the counts caught it:
# the must_fix owned ZERO, which would have shipped exactly the dead-must_fix
# defect bd-epvc1 is about, and two group rules owned 1 where they had to own 2
# because their fragment sat outside the second finding's context window.
# NSF-MESH-TEAM-JOIN-SYNC-OWN-ORIGIN-SWALLOWED owned 1 and is RETIRED with its
# twin NSF-MESH-FOREGROUND-SYNC-OWN-ORIGIN-SWALLOWED below: both defects are
# fixed (bd-1jpg7), the `.unwrap_or_default()` their findings were detected on
# is gone from both functions, so both rules would now own ZERO -- which this
# gate fails on, and which is the dead-rule state bd-epvc1 names.
3	NSF-MESH-TEAM-IDENTITY-USER-ID-ROUNDTRIP

# bd-apvhh burn-down tranche 4: the 25 findings in the 7 no-rule files left
# after tranche 3. This is the EASY REMAINDER by construction -- tranche 3 took
# the two hardest files first -- so the 15 allows here carry the same sampling
# bias tranche 1 did, and the two must_fix rules are the exception rather than
# the refutation.
#
# All 17 owned their declared counts on the first attempt, unlike tranche 3.
# The reason is visible in the fragments: every one names a whole statement or a
# distinctive method chain rather than a bare combinator.

# always; the per-rule delta across all 378 pre-existing rules showed none moved.
#
# SIX OF THESE THIRTEEN OWNED ZERO ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT, and the cause was a
# repeat of a mistake I had already made and already recorded in tranche 3: I
# passed four arguments to the five-argument allowed_in, so the fragment was read
# as the FUNCTION and the reason as the fragment. In Rust that is a compile
# error, not a silent miss -- but the ownership delta surfaced it first, before
# any build. A seventh owned zero for a subtler reason: the function was
# `audited_source_memory_ids_for_rule_candidate` and I had copied
# `audited_source_memory_ids_for_rule` out of a TRUNCATED console display. A
# truncated field used as a key is the same class as piping an existence check
# through `head`.

# The seven two-finding files (src/mesh/team.rs excepted -- bd-coxn1 debt).
#
# THE +/-4 WINDOW IS A PHRASING DISCIPLINE, NOT A TOOL DEFECT. Across tranches 3
# through 5 about 17% of my rules missed on the first attempt, consistently,
# because I chose fragments by reading the surrounding CODE while
# classify_finding matches a computed context_window(lines, index) of index-4 ..
# index+5. Those are different texts, and picking from the wrong one is guessing.
# The fix is mechanical: print the finding's window and choose a line from IT.
# In this batch every window-derived fragment landed first time; the single miss
# was an argument-ORDER slip (function and fragment transposed in allowed_in),
# which is a different mistake and one the arity check does not catch because the
# count is right.
#
# AND THE CORRELATE, worth knowing before reaching for a wider fragment: A RULE
# THAT MISSES ITS WINDOW IS OFTEN A RULE THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN TWO. It happened
# on the help-text/alias rules, the two orient joins, resume topic-vs-chosen, and
# again here on decide chosen-vs-rationale. A fragment that cannot reach both
# sites is usually telling you the sites are different concepts rather than that
# you need a longer fragment.
1	NSF-CLI-PLAN-RECIPE-SAVED-ID
1	NSF-CLI-ASK-QUESTION-REQUIRED
1	NSF-CORE-DECIDE-CHOSEN-FIELD
1	NSF-CORE-DECIDE-RATIONALE-FIELD
1	NSF-CORE-HANDOFF-TOPOLOGY-POSTURE-SUFFIX
1	NSF-CORE-HANDOFF-KNOWN-BLOCKERS
2	NSF-CORE-LAB-SCALE-FIXTURE-INDEX
1	NSF-CORE-SUPPORT-TRIPWIRE-COUNT
1	NSF-CORE-SUPPORT-PACK-REPLAY-ID
1	NSF-MESH-FOREGROUND-CONTACT-FALLBACK-HELLO
1	NSF-MESH-FOREGROUND-SYNC-BINDINGS
